reviews.reasoning: The strophe boundary itself is well-formed: the self-address device at v7 (imperative plus vocative addressed to the speaker's own soul) plausibly frames the deliverance report through v9, and every WEB quotation matches source verbatim. But the row's central substrate claim -- a lexeme thread it says runs through v4, v7, and v8 -- mis-splices two of its three citations. The word cited at Ps.116.4, מַלְּטָ֥ה, is the Piel imperative 'deliver' (2nd person), not a noun meaning 'soul'; the actual 'my soul' token in that verse is נַפְשִֽׁי, the word immediately following it, omitted from the citation. The v8 citation, מִ֫מָּ֥וֶת אֶת ('from death, [direct-object marker]'), is likewise not the soul-lexeme; that word is נַפְשִׁ֗י, two words earlier in the same verse ('you delivered my soul from death'). Only the v7 citation actually contains the word the row claims to be tracking. A second, narrower defect: boundary_evidence_refs omits Ps.116.16, which is argued by name in observed_substrate_signals.

challenges.claim: observed_substrate_signals glosses מַלְּטָ֥ה (Ps.116.4) as 'my soul' and cites מִ֫מָּ֥וֶת אֶת (Ps.116.8) toward the same three-occurrence thread, but neither fragment is the lexeme meaning 'soul' -- that word is נַפְשִֽׁי / נַפְשִׁ֗י, present in both verses but not the substring actually spliced.
challenges.evidence: Word-indexed comparison of the two verses (Ps.116.4 full text: וּבְשֵֽׁם יְהוָ֥ה אֶקְרָ֑א אָנָּ֥ה יְ֝הוָ֗ה מַלְּטָ֥ה נַפְשִֽׁי; Ps.116.8 full text: כִּ֤י חִלַּ֥צְתָּ נַפְשִׁ֗י מִ֫מָּ֥וֶת אֶת עֵינִ֥י מִן דִּמְעָ֑ה אֶת רַגְלִ֥י מִדֶּֽחִי) shows מַלְּטָ֥ה = 2nd-person Piel imperative 'deliver' and מִ֫מָּ֥וֶת אֶת = 'from death, [object marker]', neither containing the noun 'soul'. The correct נַפְשִֽׁי (end of v4) and נַפְשִׁ֗י (v8, immediately after 'you delivered') splices both collate at byte tier against Ps.116.4 and Ps.116.8 respectively (spliced programmatically from verse_map_oshb.json via collate.py) -- the dispute is which word carries the claimed sense, not the byte fidelity of either splice.

reviews.reasoning: The half-strophe boundary and its central structural claim both verify: Ps.116.14's vow-payment clause is byte-identical to Ps.116.18's, and Ps.116.13's closing clause is byte-identical to Ps.116.17's -- direct comparison of the full verse texts confirms both pairs match exactly, so this row correctly identifies and anchors on Ps 116's internal doubled-vow refrain (a structure the book strategy had left flagged as unverified for this psalm). The defect sits at v16: the row cites בֶּן אֲמָתֶ֑ךָ פִּ֝תַּ֗חְתָּ לְמוֹסֵרָֽי and glosses it 'your servant, the son of your servant girl,' but the cited Hebrew span begins at 'son of your handmaid' and continues through 'you have loosed my bonds' -- while the gloss's opening words ('your servant,') translate words earlier in the verse, not part of the citation, and the citation's own second clause (the loosing of the bonds, which WEB renders 'You have freed me from my chains') is left untranslated by the gloss.
